name: Keratosis linearis-ichthyosis congenita-sclerosing keratoderma syndrome
aliases: Keratosis linearis ichthyosis congenita sclerosing keratoderma

criteria.description: Presence of keratosis linearis with follicular hyperkeratosis
Congenital ichthyosiform erythroderma or ichthyosis congenita phenotype
Sclerosing palmoplantar keratoderma with progressive skin thickening
Identification of pathogenic mutations in the TGM1 gene
Skin biopsy showing hyperkeratosis with follicular plugging and sclerotic changes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria (keratosis linearis, ichthyosis congenita, and sclerosing keratoderma) must be present for diagnosis.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for TGM1 mutations supports diagnosis but is not mandatory.

laboratory: Elevated transglutaminase-1 enzyme activity in skin biopsy
imaging: No specific imaging abnormalities; musculoskeletal imaging may show joint contractures

distinguishingFeatures: More generalized scaling without keratosis linearis
Prominent nail dystrophy with painful palmoplantar keratoderma
Lack of ichthyosis and follicular hyperkeratosis

redFlags: Rapid progression of palmoplantar sclerosis leading to functional impairment
Development of severe ectropion causing corneal damage
